BLOCKED before a driver implementation: the pinned Minitaur ROS bridge exposes legged locomotion commands but no independent stop service or action, so the R2 mobile-base contract cannot be completed honestly. The selected primary surface is the relative robot0/command/xy_cmd Float64MultiArray subscription at examples/CommandRobotRosXY/ros_interface.py:104-106 (type imported at line 42; default robotname is robot0 at line 58 and is configurable at lines 87-88). The same file publishes robot0/state/joint JointState at line 95, /state/imu Imu at line 94, /state/pose Pose at line 97, /state/currents and /state/mean_currents Float64MultiArray at lines 98-99, and /state/impossible_motion Bool at line 102; those are observations, not a stop endpoint. Its callback at examples/CommandRobotRosXY/ros_interface.py:155-177 silently replaces a wrong-length command with a default leg posture at lines 158-161 and clamps X to 0.09..0.30 and Y to -0.10..0.10 at lines 165-176. examples/CommandRobotRosXY/command.py:80 packs x1..x4 then y1..y4 plus a restart bool, and line 87 writes that packet to /dev/ttyUSB0; there is no ROS acknowledgement of applied motion or of a stopped state. The only ROS service in this bridge is the Empty restart service at examples/CommandRobotRosXY/ros_interface.py:111-115. It sets a restart flag (command.py:121-124), which command.py:80 sends as the packet bool. The firmware handler at examples/CommandRobotRosXY/main.cpp:166-171 clears impossible_motion and sets R=0.14, theta=0; then main.cpp:189-199 restores the ANGLE/EXTENSION gains and position commands. README.md:90-92 says an over-current condition zeroes the PD gains and that /restart disables the safety to start a new motion. This is a re-arm of a fault response, not an operator stop, and zero PD gains is torque-off, not a controlled safe state. The firmware stop hook is empty at examples/CommandRobotRosXY/main.cpp:241-245. BehaviorMode_STOP exists in inc/SDK.h:63-65 and proto/simple.proto:252, but the ROS bridge does not wire it: examples/CommandRobotRos/command.py:67 hard-codes mode=1 (BehaviorMode_RUN), and although examples/CommandRobotRos/ros_interface.py:100 subscribes robot0/command/behaviorMode, command.py:63 reads behaviorMode and never puts it into the serial packet. The serial read has no timeout (examples/CommandRobotRosXY/command.py:38) and malformed replies are silently skipped (command.py:95-99), so there is no native error or quiescence signal to surface. CHANGELOG.md:18 mentions a 'Robot kill switch' only as a release note under the Vision 60 V2.5 section; it does not identify a Minitaur stop path, a ROS endpoint, or an independent hardware switch, so it is not used as estop_physical_ref. A RosDriver safety stop must be a fixed service or action (MHS/sdk/docs/ros-driver.md); this clone has none, and a topic publication would be transmission-only. A fake cannot supply the missing stop. No driver.py, fake.py, driver.lock.json or reference was authored, and only this missing-layout diagnostic gate is recorded; it is not executable driver evidence. No hardware was attached or run, no human review or test is claimed, and no lock record with authored_by or reviewed_by was fabricated.
